headlines.title: Trump threatens to blow Kharg Island 'to smithereens' as U.S. and Iran trade fresh strikes in the Gulf, driving up the price of oil
headlines.summary: This is the tape-mover of the morning — Brent punching through $90 with tankers getting hit in the Strait of Hormuz is a supply-shock story that touches everything: energy stocks, airlines, chemicals, and the long bond all at once. Kharg Island handles roughly 90% of Iran's oil exports, so any credible threat there sends the whole energy complex into a frenzy. Throw in the Fed's hawkish lean and you've got a double-barrel headwind for equities heading into a historically rough September.

headlines.title: U.S. Stock Futures Little Changed as Markets Weigh Warsh's Hawkish Remarks
headlines.summary: When the Fed Chair says summer's cooler inflation prints haven't moved the needle on underlying trends, the market has to reprice the September meeting — and that's exactly what's happening in the bond pit right now. Rate-sensitive sectors like utilities, REITs, and housing get hit hardest, but frankly nothing in the equity market loves a surprise hike. This one compounds the oil shock and makes the risk-reward for bulls look ugly going into month-end.

headlines.title: Apple enters John Ternus era as AI challenges and memory crunch intensify
headlines.summary: A CEO transition at the world's largest company by market cap is never a quiet event — Tim Cook stepping aside for Ternus on day one of September is a genuine leadership inflection point for AAPL, which anchors every major index. Memory price spikes are a margin headwind that hits the iPhone supply chain hard, and the AI competitive pressure from rivals means the new boss walks into a burning building on his first day. Watch how the stock trades relative to the broader selloff — it'll tell you a lot about how much goodwill Ternus gets from the Street.
